files.adapted_why: one stage added, this repo's own: `install` asserts the two promises the CMake install rule makes -- that a plain configure defaults the prefix to the user's ~/.local (read out of a throwaway configure's cache, never by installing into the home directory) and that the binary lands in <prefix>/bin and runs from there. It is in CI_DEFAULT_STAGES after `version`, and the stage list in the header block was updated with it. Everything else is the kit template verbatim.

the port gives the commit hook the fast tier's NAME instead of the kit's explicit stage list. The kit ships the explicit list on purpose; measured here it is the spelling that goes stale -- the 2026-09-22 incident in INCIDENTS.md is exactly that list falling a stage behind, and FSMTable's fast tier cost a pushed commit that clang-format would have rewritten. So: one list in tools/ci.sh, N callers naming a tier.

no stage list: the hook calls `tools/ci.sh --require-clean`, so a push runs whatever CI_DEFAULT_STAGES says. The kit ships an explicit list on purpose (so a stage cannot be silently dropped); measured here, the explicit list instead went STALE the moment a stage was added -- the push ran 11 of 12 stages and printed GATE PASSED. One definition, N callers.
